## 1. The covenant and the mountain  (`#the-covenant-and-the-mountain`)

Cited ayat: 2:63, 2:93, 4:154, 7:171

> **2:63** وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَٰقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُوا۟ مَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ

> **2:93** وَإِذْ أَخَذْنَا مِيثَٰقَكُمْ وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَكُمُ ٱلطُّورَ خُذُوا۟ مَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَٱسْمَعُوا۟ قَالُوا۟ سَمِعْنَا وَعَصَيْنَا وَأُشْرِبُوا۟ فِى قُلُوبِهِمُ ٱلْعِجْلَ بِكُفْرِهِمْ قُلْ بِئْسَمَا يَأْمُرُكُم بِهِۦٓ إِيمَٰنُكُمْ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤْمِنِينَ

> **4:154** وَرَفَعْنَا فَوْقَهُمُ ٱلطُّورَ بِمِيثَٰقِهِمْ وَقُلْنَا لَهُمُ ٱدْخُلُوا۟ ٱلْبَابَ سُجَّدًا وَقُلْنَا لَهُمْ لَا تَعْدُوا۟ فِى ٱلسَّبْتِ وَأَخَذْنَا مِنْهُم مِّيثَٰقًا غَلِيظًا

> **7:171** وَإِذْ نَتَقْنَا ٱلْجَبَلَ فَوْقَهُمْ كَأَنَّهُۥ ظُلَّةٌ وَظَنُّوٓا۟ أَنَّهُۥ وَاقِعٌۢ بِهِمْ خُذُوا۟ مَآ ءَاتَيْنَٰكُم بِقُوَّةٍ وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ مَا فِيهِ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَتَّقُونَ

### Claims

**c1** (2:63): God says that He took their covenant and raised the mountain above them, telling them to take what He had given them with strength and to remember what is in it, so that they might be mindful.

**c2** (7:171): Another passage says that He lifted the mountain above them as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall on them, and told them to take what He gave them with strength and remember what is in it.

**c3** (2:93): A later verse repeats the taking of the covenant and the raising of the mountain, and says that they said they heard and disobeyed, and that the calf was made to sink into their hearts because of their disbelief.

**c4** (4:154): A further passage says that God raised the mountain above them with their covenant, told them to enter the gate prostrating and not to transgress on the Sabbath, and took from them a solemn covenant.

### One-minute summary

God says that He took their covenant and raised the mountain above them, telling them to take what He had given them with strength and to remember what is in it [c1][c2]. Another passage adds that they were to enter the gate prostrating and not to transgress on the Sabbath [c4].

### Complete story

God says that He took their covenant and raised the mountain above them, telling them to take what He had given them with strength and to remember what is in it, so that they might be mindful [c1]. Another passage says that He lifted the mountain above them as if it were a canopy, and they thought it was going to fall on them [c2].

A later verse repeats the taking of the covenant and the raising of the mountain, and says that they said they heard and disobeyed [c3]. A further passage says that God raised the mountain above them with their covenant, told them to enter the gate prostrating and not to transgress on the Sabbath, and took from them a solemn covenant [c4].

### Deep study

The verses tell one scene from different sides: the covenant and the command [c1], the canopy and the fear that it would fall [c2], the answer they gave [c3], and the further commands of the gate and the Sabbath [c4]. The repeated reminder in the same surah is placed after a mention of the calf [c3]. Who is addressed is read from the surrounding passages; these verses say you and them [c1].

### Kids mode

God took a promise from them and lifted the mountain above them [c1][c2]. God told them to hold on to what He gave them and to remember what is in it [c1].

### Life lessons (educational interpretation)

Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the covenant is joined to a command to take what was given with strength and to remember it [c1]. Another is that the later verse records the answer they gave [c3].

### What the sources do not establish

- Not established: when this took place in relation to the tablets or the calf.
- Not established: the nature of the raising of the mountain; interpreters differ on whether it is to be taken literally.
- Not established: what the gate and the Sabbath refer to in 4:154.
- Who is addressed is read from the surrounding passages; these verses say you and them and do not name the people in this record.
- The relation between 2:63 and 2:93, a repeated reminder in the same surah, is a matter for scholars.
- The inventory also treats these verses as one event; the verses themselves do not say that the passages are one scene (an inference).
